$description: P3 exemptions (docs/evidence-edges.md). A non-enforced claim may keep an absolute quantifier ONLY with a reason recorded here, so an exemption is a reviewable artifact rather than a silent weakening. Key is `<claimId>:<word>`; the value is the reason and must be non-empty. check-overclaim.mjs also fails a STALE entry — one whose word no longer appears in that claim's text — because a dead exemption reads as a live judgement. Adding an entry to quiet the gate, without a reason that survives reading, is the overclaim this check exists to prevent.
c4:never: Held after review, not waived. c4 is graded PARTIAL, but its gap places the partiality in TRANSPORT STRENGTH — 'on macOS the broker listens on TCP loopback — weaker than unix-socket possession' — not in whether the agent holds credentials. On that point the gap AFFIRMS the claim: 'keeperd/daemon.ts holds the key; claude-box is credential-free.' So 'never holds the credential' is accurate at the partial grade; what is partial is how strongly the broker's endpoint is isolated, which the gap already discloses. Revisit if a gap ever lands saying the agent CAN hold a credential — then the word must go, not the entry.
